translation.english_text: Yes, yes! That's me. Do you doubt even that?... Hmm... You're thinking about what I looked like twenty years ago! I'm thinking about what you'll look like twenty years from now... Hmm... ‘all things come turning, like a cord...’—leave that, you donkey.... (Going to her) Then shall I go and come back? I asked if I may go and come back... (He goes, then returns) I forgot to ask. What are you cooking today? I'm asking what you're cooking today...
notes: The source phrase `சராசரங்கள் வரும் சுழன்றே சரடுபோல் அருகாடான்னா` is difficult and elliptical in context; the English preserves its discernible image conservatively rather than inventing a completed saying.

The internal directions and spoken continuation belong to the same labelled Punyakodi utterance `tirumbippaar-s051-d001`; historical split units u002/u003 have therefore been removed without renumbering the remaining IDs.

translation.english_text: Radha! No more of this trouble from now on. I married out of desire only to end up suffering.... (Taking paper and pencil) Here, keep this paper. Keep this pencil stub. For everything, show me by writing it down.
From now on, show me everything by writing it down! Shall I go and come back, Radha? I asked if I may go and come back... Forget it! (He leaves.)
